newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan market led by cement stock demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordan market led by cement stock demand.

text.p: Jordanian shares inched to a slightly higher close on Tuesday in quiet activity focused on foreign-inspired demand for a cement firm, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.14 percent to 164.70 points on turnover worth 673,201 dinars ($949,507).
Dealers said excess stock above demand rumoured to have been foreign-inspired helped drag Jordan Cement Factories 0.03 dinars lower to 3.94 dinars in busy trade worth 122,833 dinars.
"The market was very quiet with no strong demand and most of the trade was focused on cement and drug firms," said Ibrahim Odeh, broker at Wataniyeh Financial Services.
There was hardly any other trade aside from some activity on National Chlorine and Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturing which were fuelled by local investor interest.
Heavyweight Arab Bank, which drove the official index up to a three-year high earlier in July, rose 1.50 dinars to 290 dinars in trade of just 60 shares.
Local investors piled into the shares in recent weeks, anticipating strong 1997 profits, announcement of a bonus share offering and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
But cancellation of the 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling has been delayed in cabinet, deflating the Arab Bank bubble.
Overall sixteen shares rose on Tuesday and 15 fell with another 13 trading but closing unchanged.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, rose 0.03 percent to 80.49 points, 3.48 percent down since the start of the year. $1 = 0.709 dinars
